claim: ACP gene expression increased significantly after 1 hour of sustained flight.
source: The mRNA levels of four neuropeptide precursor genes, namely, AKH/corazonin-related peptide (ACP), adipokinetic hormone (AKH2), NPF1, and GPB5, changed significantly after flying treatment. Among these genes, three (ACP, AKH2, and NPF1) exhibited clearly increased expression levels, whereas GPB5 displayed decreased expression levels after 1 h- of sustained flight (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript reports qPCR data showing gene expression changes after sustained flight.

claim: A homozygous ACP mutant line with a 13 bp deletion was successfully generated using CRISPR/Cas9.

claim: ACP peptide is detected in neurons of the pars intercerebralis and bilateral forebrain of wild-type locusts.

evidence: The manuscript reports immunohistochemistry results shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Flight is one of the most intense and energy-demanding physiological processes, especially for insects with long-term flight capacity.
source: Despite these adaptive advantages, flight is one of the most intense and energy-demanding physiological processes, especially for insects that possess long-term flight capacity, such as locusts and butterflies (Mentel et al., 2003; Zhan et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript cites published literature to support this statement.

claim: Metabolic rates in the flight muscle can increase by 20- to 100-fold during flight.
source: Metabolic rates in the flight muscle can increase by 20- to 100-fold during flight (Harrison and Roberts, 2000; Suarez, 2000).
evidence: The manuscript cites published literature to support this statement.

claim: Short-term flight exclusively employs carbohydrates as energy substrates.
source: Compared to short-term flight, which exclusively employs carbohydrates as energy substrates, many physiological activities subsequently occur in the flight muscle during long-term flight, including carbohydrate/lipid metabolism transition, fatty acid transport, lipid oxidation, and lipid mobilization in the fat body.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge about insect flight metabolism.

claim: Long-term flight involves carbohydrate/lipid metabolism transition, fatty acid transport, lipid oxidation, and lipid mobilization in the fat body.
source: Compared to short-term flight, which exclusively employs carbohydrates as energy substrates, many physiological activities subsequently occur in the flight muscle during long-term flight, including carbohydrate/lipid metabolism transition, fatty acid transport, lipid oxidation, and lipid mobilization in the fat body.
evidence: The manuscript states this as established knowledge about insect flight metabolism.

claim: Most neuropeptides are produced by the central nervous system and perform distinct tasks through binding with their cognate G-protein-coupled receptors.
source: Most neuropeptides are produced by the central nervous system and perform distinct tasks through binding with their cognate G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) (Nässel, 2002).
evidence: The manuscript cites published literature to support this statement.

claim: AKH has been demonstrated to be a conserved regulator of flight-related energy metabolism by promoting glycolysis and lipid mobilization in the fat body in different insect species.
source: For example, adipokinetic hormone (AKH) has been demonstrated to be a conserved regulator of flight-related energy metabolism by promoting glycolysis and lipid mobilization in the fat body in different insect species (Gäde et al., 2006; Kaufmann and Brown, 2008).
evidence: The manuscript cites published literature to support this statement.

claim: The migratory locust possesses a notable long-term flight capacity and is one of the most destructive agricultural pests.
source: The migratory locust, Locusta migratoria, which possesses a notable long-term flight capacity, is one of the most destructive agricultural pests (Wang and Kang, 2014) and has been employed as a useful study model for the neurohormonal regulation of flight-related energy metabolism (Jutsum and Goldsworthy, 1976; Van der Horst and Rodenburg, 2010; Bullard et al., 2017).
evidence: The manuscript cites published literature to support this statement.

claim: During the early stage of flight, carbohydrates in flight muscle and hemolymph significantly decrease.
source: Usually, metabolism involved in long-term flight in insects contains two major phases: during the early stage of flight, carbohydrates in flight muscle and hemolymph significantly decrease, and lipid mobilization in the fat body gradually increases thereafter followed by utilization in the flight muscle during the prolonged flight phase (Worm and Beenakkers, 1980; Wegener et al., 1986), indicating a clear transition in energy consumption from carbohydrates to lipids during long-term flight.
evidence: The manuscript cites published literature to support this statement.

claim: Lipid mobilization in the fat body gradually increases during prolonged flight followed by utilization in the flight muscle.
